Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
PHP-CFH-25-001, Healthy Babies Healthy Children Program Update
notes:
Grace Bermingham, Director Child, Family & Dental Health, introduced Janet McCreary, Manager Child & Family Health and the presentation on Healthy Babies, Healthy Children program which plays a critical role in supporting upstream health. A copy of the presentation is attached to original agenda. J. McCreary provided a presentation on the Healthy Babies and Healthy Children program and its achievements in 2024. She highlighted that the program had an increase in funding in 2024 which will allow service expansions such as bedside screening, at-home assessments, additional hours, and additional medical Staff. In 2024, there were 276 families supported with home visits to assist in various ways, such as healthy growth and development, childcare, mental health assistance. She also highlighted several lived experience accounts of Community Members successfully utilizing the program and that 93% of respondents were satisfied with the program.

The Committee acknowledged the positive impact of the program on the Community.

In response to the Committee, J. McCreary explained that only 74% of families participate in the bedside screening as it is an optional program and due to the hours of operation some babies are born outside of the scheduled times and families are less likely to engage if contacted via phone. She further explained that the screening tool was developed in 2012 and will be assessed by program leaders province-wide to ensure its effectiveness. Currently, Staff use the screening tool and their judgment to address any key concerns for all Members of the Community.

In further response to the Committee, J. McCreary confirmed that the program encourages breastfeeding, especially for the first six months. 

Received for information.

items.title: Stephen Litt, Vive Development Corporation
notes:
Stephen Litt, Vive Development Corporation, provided a presentation on the proposed Housing Innovation Project. A copy of the presentation is attached to original agenda. He gave a brief background on their corporate mandate which is to focus on purpose-built rentals that can be constructed at lower prices to create housing options for moderate income households. The proposed project is aimed at a partnership between both the public and private sectors to create mid-market housing. He highlighted that the proposed housing project at 140 Weber Street has potential cost savings of $25.8 million and could increase available units from 35 to 210. He further highlighted that the units available would be mixed income which promotes sustainable living.

In response to the Committee, S. Litt confirmed that each project is different in terms of unit cost and the proposed innovation project is to include affordable housing units at an average cost of $800.00.

Responding to the Committee, Peter Sweeney, Commissioner Community Services, provided a brief synopsis on the Waterloo Regional Housing Revitalization plan which will explore new partnership opportunities and operating models for the project on Weber Street. Staff will be working on a public request for proposals in 2025.
